decisions.reason: As a close extension of the core practice software and even framed as a new product line, it likely meets the firm's aspiration level well enough to retain under a growing firm's available slack.

The education institute fits the firm's support and training capabilities, so even if returns are somewhat less visible than software sales, its strategic fit and the firm's growth make continued retention more likely than withdrawal.

Remote screen-sharing support is adjacent to the established support business and can strengthen customer retention, so boundedly rational management would likely keep it unless results clearly fall short of aspirations.
A practice analytics dashboard matches the firm's direction toward digital and efficient practice management, making it a plausible satisfier relative to peer and past innovation aspirations.

A complete dental practice bundle is very close to the established offer and likely supports cross-selling and standardization, so it is the least likely of the new products to be taken off the market.

The job and practice listing portal is the most distant from the firm's core software business, so if its performance is ambiguous or below aspiration, management is most likely to reallocate those resources to closer and more certain opportunities.
